lina (support): FYI customer-omega reported p99 jumps to ~4.2s on text-generation API since ~08:10 UTC. They also see GPU OOMs in their logs and some requests falling back to a slower model. Ticket #CS-4982.

raj (eng-sre): Can you paste the error lines and which model variant they're hitting?

lina (support): Root log snippet from their agent: 
```
[2026-03-12T08:11:02Z] ERROR model-runner: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-12T08:11:02Z] WARN model-runner: falling back to cpu backend for request id=abc123
[2026-03-12T08:11:02Z] INFO kv-cache: entries=4.1M total_bytes=3.3G per_gpu=1.1G
```
They were on `redwood-3b-v2` hosted variant, steady traffic ~120 rps at the time.

sophia (eng-runtime): Noted. Any recent rollouts around 08:00? deploy-bot: release `runtime/2026.03.12-08` deployed to us-west-2 at 07:58 UTC :deploy:

raj (eng-sre): Pinged oncall. Paging raj. :pager:

raj (eng-sre): I'm on it. Lina, can you share the metrics (prometheus query) for `inference_gpu_memory_total_bytes` and `inference_kv_entries` for the pod ids?

lina (support): Curated metrics from customer (they gave us a sanitized dump):
```
# time series snapshot around the incident
inference_gpu_memory_used_bytes{pod="r3-12-7"} 1.05e9
inference_kv_entries{pod="r3-12-7"} 4096000
worker_heap_alloc{pod="r3-12-7"} 280MB
worker_tcmalloc_frag_ratio{pod="r3-12-7"} 1.92
```

devon (eng-runtime): frag_ratio ~1.9 is high. That aligns with fragmentation causing repeated `cudaMalloc` failures even though used memory < gpu capacity. Also kv entries ~4M is unusually large for this workload. Any change in average generated tokens per request?

lina (support): Customer says they updated chat UI the day before to store the full conversation history client-side, and the new client now sends the full history in each request (longer prompt lengths). They only realized yesterday.

sophia (eng-runtime): That would explain KV growth: per-request KV caches are proportional to prompt+generated tokens. If the client now sends full convo each call, average KV entries per request can spike. Combined with allocator fragmentation -> p99 regressions and OOMs.

raj (eng-sre): Quick triage plan: 1) throttle heavy requests from that customer to prevent immediate OOM cascading; 2) roll deterministic restarts for the model workers experiencing high frag_ratio; 3) add a temporary server-side cap on per-request kv retention for hosted tier.

devon (eng-runtime): I can do (2) and (3). For (3) runtime flag we can flip `--kv-cache-max-entries-per-request=20000` which prunes KV after X entries; current default is unlimited. That should prevent runaway growth while we work the longer fix.

sophia (eng-runtime): Before restarting, can we inspect `nvidia-smi` + driver allocator logs to ensure we don't trigger preemptive OOM kill of other tenants? Lina, ask the customer for `nvidia-smi -q` and `dmesg | tail -n 80`.

lina (support): Requested. They sent this small snippet: 
```
NVRM: GPU memory fragmentation 43%
NVRM: Tainted: PERSISTENT
kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4421 (model-worker) score 987
```

raj (eng-sre): 43% fragmentation is consistent with tcmalloc/jemalloc and many small allocations. Short-term mitigation = rolling restart to reclaim memory and reduce fragmentation. Long-term = allocator tuning + proactive defrag path.

devon (eng-runtime): I'm going to push the kv-cap and an autoscaler tweak to reduce concurrency for r3-12-7 pool (scale down heavy concurrency by 30% for worker class long-gen). Applying to us-west-2 now.

deploy-bot: Starting rolling config change `kv-cap-2026-03-12` to us-west-2...

sophia (eng-runtime): Also set an ingress policy to route the customer's API key to the smaller context-length variant for now (redwood-3b-v2-shortctx) to prevent further growth. Lina, can you request the customer to opt-in? If they refuse, we'll rate-limit to protect overall SLOs.

lina (support): Reached out to customer, they agreed to try the shortctx variant for a few hours.

devon (eng-runtime): Config changes applied: `--kv-cache-max-entries-per-request=20000` and concurrency cap on the pool. Rolling restart of affected workers started (one-at-a-time).

raj (eng-sre): After first restart I see frag_ratio drop to 1.12 on r3-12-7-01. p99 decreased from 4.2s -> 1.6s for that shard. Prometheus snapshot: 
```
inference_p99_latency_ms{pod="r3-12-7-01"} 1600
inference_gpu_memory_used_bytes{pod="r3-12-7-01"} 9.6e8
worker_tcmalloc_frag_ratio{pod="r3-12-7-01"} 1.12
```

lina (support): Customer confirmed latency improved for their test traffic after switching to shortctx. They still want to send full convo though - they need help with a server-side approach.

sophia (eng-runtime): Long term we should: 1) implement server-side automatic prompt truncation/compaction when prompts exceed per-customer configured context length; 2) introduce proactive KV eviction policy (LRU-ish for prefix tokens); 3) add a defragmentation path in the runtime that coalesces GPU allocations during idle windows; 4) expose `kv_entries` per-request in the dashboard so customers can see their impact.

devon (eng-runtime): On allocator side, experiment options: switch jemalloc tunables or re-enable our internal `defrag()` in the CUDA allocator. There's also a kernel-level CUDA driver patch (NVIDIA 535.x -> 540.x) that helped fragmentation for other vendors, but it needs validation.

raj (eng-sre): I'll open an incident summary and timeline for CS and execs. Short-term mitigations applied: kv-cap + routing + rolling restarts + rate-limit for the customer's key.

lina (support): Customer asked for timeline on the permanent fix. Can we get an ETA?

sophia (eng-runtime): ETA tentative: 2 weeks to ship server-side prompt compaction and kv eviction; 4-6 weeks for allocator defrag + kernel upgrade validation. We'll prioritise compaction and dashboard visibility first.

devon (eng-runtime): Logging follow-ups: create a regression test that simulates repeated long-prefix requests to reproduce kv growth and fragmentation in CI, so future runtime changes don't regress this. I'll add the test.

raj (eng-sre): Added `INC-2026-0312-oom-p99` with links to metrics, logs, and the customer ticket. Assigning follow-ups: Sophia=design compaction, Devon=allocator experiment+test, Raj=driver/infra validation + incident writeup, Lina=customer comms.

lina (support): Customer happy with shortctx and the temporary cap for now. They'll try a client change but asked us to implement server-side protections. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

sophia (eng-runtime): Thanks everyone. We'll track progress in the incident doc and update CS with the 2-week plan.

devon (eng-runtime): I'll post PRs and a reproducer link in the incident.

raj (eng-sre): Closing immediate pager. Marking as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:

alerts-bot: Alert resolved: high-p99-inference-us-west-2 (incident id INC-2026-0312-oom-p99)
